questions.q: What does the 'As of' timestamp in a Lightning dashboard header tell you?
options: When the dashboard was created
When the data was last refreshed
When the running user last logged in
When the next subscription email will send
questions.explain: Dashboards are not real-time. The timestamp shows the last refresh, so an old one is a cue to refresh.

questions.q: Which of these is typically chosen in the Subscribe dialog?
options: Frequency, days and time, and recipients
The object the dashboard queries
The field-level security of the report
The org's data storage limit
questions.explain: You choose how often, on which days and time, and who receives the dashboard, subject to your permissions.

questions.q: Why would you add a condition to a report subscription?
options: To change the report's source object
To hide the report from other users
To make the report refresh in real time
So it only sends when something meaningful is true, like a record count above zero
questions.explain: Conditions let the email act as light alerting, arriving only when the report meets your threshold.

questions.q: Whose data does a scheduled dashboard refresh use?
options: Each recipient's own access
The dashboard's running user
No one's; it uses an anonymous system view
Whoever clicked Subscribe last
questions.explain: The refresh runs under the running user, so recipients see what that user can see. That is why you review data before adding a wide audience.

questions.q: Which statement about subscription limits is the safest to teach?
options: Every edition allows unlimited subscriptions
Subscriptions can never be used on reports
Limits are identical across all editions and never change
Editions limit the number of scheduled refreshes and subscriptions, so check your own org's limits
questions.explain: Limits vary by edition, so verify them in your org instead of assuming.
